boards.school_name: SUNY College of Environmental Science and Forestry
boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented ESF customs centered on the Quad, the enduring fictional student Eustace B. Nifkin, and senior class gifts.

cards.title: Don’t Cut Across the Quad
cards.subtitle: ESF Quad
cards.notes: Take the surrounding paths instead of using the lawn as a shortcut. The custom protects the Quad’s open green space from worn footpaths.
cards.short_summary: A campus rule of thumb that keeps the central lawn intact.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF says students do not walk or “cut” across the Quad in order to preserve it as open green space without worn paths.
cards.access_notes: Observe from the paths; do not cross the lawn as a shortcut.

cards.title: The Quad Has Its Own Heckle
cards.subtitle: ESF Quad
cards.notes: If someone cuts across the lawn, expect the traditional reminder from nearby campus community members: “Get off the Quad!”
cards.short_summary: A vocal enforcement mechanism for the no-cutting custom.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF documents that cutting across the Quad earns quick notice, including people shouting “Get off the Quad!”
cards.access_notes: Keep the reminder good-natured and respect others’ space.

cards.title: Meet ESF’s Unofficial Student
cards.subtitle: Campus-wide tradition
cards.notes: Look for references to Eustace B. Nifkin, ESF’s long-running fictional student, and treat the joke as a piece of shared campus history.
cards.short_summary: A fictional student who has been part of campus lore since the 1940s.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF identifies Eustace B. Nifkin as its unofficial student and says he first appeared on campus during the 1940s.
cards.access_notes: A historical campus tradition; no special access required.

cards.entity_name: Eustace B. Nifkin on Class Rosters
cards.title: The Student Who Appears on Paperwork
cards.subtitle: Campus records tradition
cards.notes: Notice the recurring gag when Eustace’s name turns up on class rosters or official College documents, despite no known explanation.
cards.short_summary: The fictional student’s name has a documented habit of entering official-looking records.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF says Eustace B. Nifkin’s name appears on class rosters and other official College documents.
cards.access_notes: View as campus lore; do not alter College records or forms.

cards.title: Find the Lounge Named for Nifkin
cards.subtitle: Marshall Hall
cards.notes: When visiting Marshall Hall’s student lounge, recognize its common Nifkin Lounge name as a lasting tribute to ESF’s fictional student.
cards.short_summary: A real student lounge carries the unofficial student’s name.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF states that the student lounge in Marshall Hall is commonly called Nifkin Lounge in Eustace’s honor.
cards.access_notes: Follow current Marshall Hall building-access rules.

cards.title: The Diploma That Didn’t End the Joke
cards.subtitle: Eustace B. Nifkin tradition
cards.notes: Share the improbable graduation lore carefully: ESF says Eustace received a SUNY diploma in 1972, then supposedly pursued another degree.
cards.short_summary: The fictional student is said to have graduated—and returned.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF documents that Eustace received a SUNY diploma in 1972 and says he evidently returned to work on a second degree.
cards.access_notes: A historical tradition described by ESF.

cards.title: Postcards From an Invisible Classmate
cards.subtitle: Eustace B. Nifkin tradition
cards.notes: Keep an eye out for the campus legend’s global correspondence: ESF says Eustace sends mail back to the College from around the world.
cards.short_summary: A fictional student’s reported postcards extend the campus joke beyond Syracuse.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF says the well-traveled Eustace B. Nifkin sends mail to ESF from all over the world.
cards.access_notes: Treat this as historic campus lore; do not use College addresses without permission.

cards.title: A Past Senior Send-Off Cameo
cards.subtitle: Commencement tradition
cards.notes: When discussing graduation lore, note that ESF documents a past practice of seniors finding ways to include Eustace in commencement celebrations.
cards.short_summary: The fictional student has appeared in past senior celebrations.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF says that, in the past, seniors included Eustace B. Nifkin somehow in their commencement celebrations.
cards.access_notes: Documented as a past practice; it is not presented as a current commencement instruction.

cards.title: Eustace’s Socially Significant Other
cards.subtitle: Campus-wide tradition
cards.notes: Learn the companion legend: students in the early 1970s connected the initials E.S.F. around campus to Elsa S. Freeborn.
cards.short_summary: A fictional counterpart expands ESF’s long-running initials-based lore.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF says students in the early 1970s discovered E.S.F. initials around campus and identified Elsa S. Freeborn as Eustace’s Socially Significant Other.
cards.access_notes: A historical campus legend; no special access required.

cards.title: Leave a Class Gift Behind
cards.subtitle: Senior-class tradition
cards.notes: As graduation approaches, explore the record of senior gifts—from the Marshall Hall clock to environmental projects—that commemorate each departing class.
cards.short_summary: Departing classes traditionally mark their time at ESF with a gift to the College.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF says senior classes traditionally make a gift to the College, listing examples including the Marshall Hall clock and retired air-pollution credits.
cards.access_notes: Participation and contribution practices may vary by class; consult current class-gift organizers.
